page: Amazon Web Services m5d.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose instance featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 8175M processors running at 3.1 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per physical core. This instance includes 3600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, showing strong results for both small-block cached reads at 4545.24 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 216.75 GB/sec. Database operations are a key strength, with Redis SET operations reaching 76.56 million operations per second and static web serving throughput measured at 48.67 GB/sec.

While multi-core and database benchmarks are strong, single-core performance is average, as shown by Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core metrics. Additionally, without dedicated GPU hardware, the instance exhibits poor performance in LLM text generation, scoring in the bottom 10% for small and medium models. Qualitatively, the bare-metal configuration offers high resource density and direct hardware access, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high memory bandwidth and local NVMe storage without virtualization overhead.

This hardware profile is suited for large-scale database deployments, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and multi-threaded software compilation. It is also appropriate for general-purpose enterprise applications requiring high-capacity local storage and high network throughput.
